subject: sociology
title: Explaining Why People Offend
welcome_lead: From Merton's strain to Becker's labels, meet the studies that explain why some people break the rules.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology adventure on Merton's strain theory, labelling, gender and Marxist views of crime.
final_note: Strong AO2 answers name one theorist per perspective and a clear study.

concepts.def: Merton: crime when goals exceed legal means.
Normlessness; rules feel weak or unclear.
Becker: deviance is created by who is labelled.
Label that overrides all other identities.
Claim courts treat women more leniently.
Unreported, unrecorded crime missing from stats.

walkthroughs.body_html: Merton argued society pushes everyone toward goals like wealth but blocks legal routes for the poor. This strain produces innovation — using illegal means like theft to reach legitimate goals.
Becker's Outsiders argued no act is inherently deviant — it becomes deviant when powerful groups label it. The label can become a master status, pushing the person into a deviant career.

Carlen (1988) found working-class women turn to crime when 'class deal' and 'gender deal' break down. Chambliss showed Marxist crime: laws protect the wealthy, while crimes of the poor are policed more heavily.
